name: Question 6
problem:
Use mathematical induction to prove that
${[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{n}=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{n} & {2}^{n}-1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$
for all $n\in N.$

We proceed using induction on $n.$

**Base Case**: We first prove that our statement is true for the base case $n=$ {{field-1}}.

For the left-hand side, we have

$$
{{field-2}}={{field-3}}
$$

and for the right-hand side, we have

$$
{{field-4}}={{field-5}}.
$$

Thus, our statement is {{field-6}} for $n=1.$

**Inductive Hypothesis**: We assume that for some $n=$ {{field-7}}, we have

$$
{{field-8}}={{field-9}}.
$$

**Inductive Step**: To prove $P(k+1),$ we write

$$
\begin{aligned}{{field-10}} & ={{field-11}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

By the inductive hypothesis, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{k}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & ={{field-12}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{field-13}} \\  & ={{field-14}},\end{aligned}
$$

as required.

Therefore, by the principle of induction,
${[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{n}=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{n} & {2}^{n}-1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$
is true for all {{field-15}}.
